description: Statically inventory the GPU code in a CUDA program (ADR-0006): from a host ELF/PE with a .nv_fatbin section, a standalone fatbin, cubin or PTX file, the fatbin containers and entries (PTX or cubin, target architecture sm_NN, compression: zstd and LZ4 payloads are read under size caps), and per kernel its mangled name, code size, register count, constant/shared/local memory and an instruction estimate; PTX version, target and kernel names. Parses only: no SASS decoding, no CUDA toolkit or driver, nothing is run, and nothing is written. Names from the file are untrusted text and are screened by AIDefence (redactedCount / screened report this). Use when you need the GPU side of a CUDA program (which architectures it targets, whether it ships PTX, which kernels exist and what each costs): rure_analyze_binary alone only shows the .nv_fatbin section names, and grep or strings find kernel names only by chance. Run rure_analyze_binary first when it is not known whether a file holds CUDA code.

includePtx.description: Also return the PTX text, cut at 64 KiB (default false)

path.description: Absolute path to a CUDA host binary (ELF/PE), a .fatbin, a .cubin or a .ptx file

name: rure_analyze_cuda
